item.content:encoded:
The Saline Home Builders Association is preparing to host its 2026 “Fore the Builders” Golf Tournament on Thursday, Sept. 17, at the Hurricane Golf & Country Club.

The upcoming community event features two separate flights, meals for participants, and various prize opportunities. Read more below.




The tournament will host two scheduled flights for teams. Morning participants can check in and enjoy breakfast during the 8 a.m. registration period, with the first flight officially teeing off at 8:30 a.m.

Afternoon players will have a separate registration and lunch starting at noon, followed by the second flight at 1 p.m.

The team entry fee is set at $450. Additionally, attendees can purchase a separate game package for $60. The tournament will conclude with the distribution of prizes and awards to the participating golfers.

Those interested in registering a team or seeking further information about the event can contact Amy with the Saline Home Builders Association by calling 501-909-8055 or emailing salinehba@gmail.com.

item.content:encoded:
Habitat for Humanity will present their second annual Murder Mystery Dinner Theater. This fun fundraiser will have dinner and a show, along with pre-show hors d’oevres. There will also be a silent and live auction, and casino games.




Sponsored by Ridout Lumber Company and Saline County Home Builders Association, the event is set for Thursday, October 15th at the Hill Barn Event Center on 100 Hill Road in Bryant. That’s off Reynolds Road and adjacent to Hill Barn Elementary School.

Doors open at 6PM, dinner and show begins at 7PM and the auctions and casino games continue the evening at 8PM.

Watch for information on tickets and more at https://habitatsalinecounty.com/.

item.content:encoded:
Organizers have released ticket sales dates and a complete schedule of events for the upcoming 2026 Salt Bowl rivalry matchup between the Benton Panthers and Bryant Hornets. Tickets go on sale August 17 and the game is Friday, August 28, at Hornet Stadium. Local fans can now prepare for game-week pep rallies, community blood drives, and charity donation contests. Read more below.




Salt Bowl 2026 – Benton vs. Bryant
7:00 p.m., Friday, August 28th, 2026
Hornet Stadium (map)
“Stars, Stripes and Friday Night Lights”

The Salt Bowl Committee is pleased to announce that Salt Bowl 2026 will be “Stars, Stripes and Friday Night Lights” Celebrating America’s 250th Birthday! The largest high school football game in the State of Arkansas will be played on Friday night, August 28th, at 7:00 pm at Hornet Stadium in Bryant.

SPONSORS

The Presenting Sponsor of Salt Bowl 2026 is Everett Buick GMC, and joining them as sponsors of this year’s game are Jones Heating and Air, Bryant Family Pharmacy, and First Security Bank.

GAME WEEK – AUG 24-28

Game week will kick-off on Monday August 24th with the beginning of the annual Salt Bowl Peanut Butter Drive that is always a great competition between the schools and both districts, the drive will run through the end of September. Be sure to send peanut butter to your favorite school in each district.

CHARITY DONATION DRIVES

The Salt Bowl Committee is pleased to once again work with great organizations to give back to our community:  the Arkansas Blood Institute and Goodwill Industries of Arkansas, and we will also have the annual Salt Bowl Peanut Butter Drive that we will begin the week of Salt Bowl and go throughout the month of September.

Our Blood Institute will be holding Special Salt Bowl Community Blood Drives. The Benton Community Blood Drive is 10 am-5 pm on Monday August 24th, at the River Center. The Bryant Community Drive is from 10 am-5 pm Tuesday August 25th at Bishop Park, Court 1. The community that donates the most blood will receive a very large trophy to display at their community center. Details on the special promotions and links to schedule appointments can be found by visiting https://obi.org/events/blood-drive-blitz/

High School Blood Drives: The Benton High School Blood Drive is from 9:00 am-2:00 pm on Monday August 31st, in the ROTC room, and the Bryant High School Blood Drive is from 9 am-2 pm on Thursday, September 10th, in the Multi-Purpose Room.  The districts will be competing for a trophy for the school that donates the most pints of blood. The winner of the High School Blood Drive will be announced during the Saline County Shootout on December 18th at Panther Arena.

Goodwill Industries of Arkansas is another strong partner of Salt Bowl. Beginning Monday August 17th through Thursday August 27th, Goodwill stores in Benton and Bryant will collect Salt Bowl donations. Students, families, and the community are encouraged to donate gently used clothing and household items at their respective Goodwill locations. In addition to helping fund numerous programs that provide education, training, and employment assistance, donations collected will mean money for the school districts and gift cards for families in need. Fans can also make a monetary donation at GoodwillAR.org, designating the school to support.

The donations will be totaled, and the winning district will be named at the game. The district with the most donations will receive a check for $1,500, along with $500 in gift cards to give to families in need. The second-place district will also receive $500 in gift cards, plus a check for $1,000.

SHIRTS

Salt Bowl 2026 T-shirts can be purchased at  https://crxted.com/saltbowl. T-Shirts, tank tops, toddler and infant apparel are also available now.

PEP RALLIES – AUG 25

Once again both teams will be having community pep rallies for football and volleyball at 6:00pm on Tuesday night August 25th Benton will be at Everett Infiniti and Bryant will be at Everett Buick GMC along Interstate 30 directly across from each other.

PRESS CONFERENCE – AUG 26

On Wednesday the 26th we will have the Annual Coaches’ and Players’ press conference and Benton and Bryant Chamber luncheon sponsored by First Security Bank held from 11:30am to 1pm at the Saline County Career and Technical Campus-ASU Three Rivers and via Zoom. Coach Brad Harris, Coach Quad Sanders and players from each team will be available for interviews about this year’s game. A Zoom link will be sent to the members of the media prior to the press conference.

VOLLEYBALL BATTLE – AUG 27

The Annual Battle of the BTowns Volleyball Game will be on Thursday night with the Bryant Lady Hornets Volleyball team taking on the multiple State Champion Benton Lady Panthers at Panther Arena at 5 pm.

TICKETS

Benton ticket info:  Parents and guardians of Benton football, cheer, dance, and band students will have the opportunity to purchase two tickets through their child’s coach or director. Benton High School students may purchase one ticket per student during the first week of school. All previously held reserved seating will be honored, and AAA passes will be accepted for general admission only. General admission tickets will go on sale Monday, August 17, 2026, at the south ticket box of Everett Field at Panther Stadium from 9 a.m. to 1:30 p.m., or until sold out. Tickets are $15 each, CASH ONLY (no checks or debit cards), with a limit of four tickets per family. Ticket sales are first come, first-served and are for Benton Patrons. Benton patrons will receive maroon, Benton-branded tickets.

Bryant ticket info:  Parents/guardians of Bryant football travel team players, cheer, dance, and band students can purchase 2 tickets through their student’s coach or director. Bryant patrons will receive blue, Bryant-branded tickets. Bryant High School students may purchase one ticket during lunch beginning Monday, August 17. Seniors will have the first opportunity to purchase tickets.

General admission tickets will go on sale Monday August 17th 2026 at the Hornet Stadium ticket booth from 10am-2pm or until sold out. Tickets are $15 each, CASH ONLY, with a limit of two tickets per person. AAA passes are accepted for general admission only.

TAILGATE

You will not need a game ticket to attend the Tailgate Party. If you do have a ticket, the gates will open at 6pm and Benton fans must use the Benton gate which will be on the east side of Hornet Stadium, and Bryant fans must use the Bryant gate on the north side of the stadium.

PAY-PER-VIEW STREAMING

There will be a Pay-Per-View option for this year’s game. More information on how to purchase the game will be released closer to game day.

TAILGATE

This year’s event will include the annual Arkansas’ Largest High School Tailgate Party, featuring over 70 vendors and organizations from across Saline County. It will kick off at 4 pm on the East and North Side of Hornet Stadium. Anyone interested in renting a booth space should contact Dee Ann Shepard at the Bryant Athletic Office dshepard@bryantschools.org, 501-653-5151. Vendor Booths will close at 7 pm.

KICKOFF & HALFTIME

The Rob Patrick Award will be presented prior to kickoff of the game and at halftime, the Legacy of Bryant and Bryant Varsity Dance will perform.

MAGAZINE

Also hitting the newsstands is the annual Salt Bowl Edition of the Saline County Lifestyles Magazine, be sure to look for one around town.

UPDATES

For updates regarding this year’s game, fans can visit each school’s athletic website, our Facebook page, Twitter, and Instagram @SaltBowlAR. Comment using the hashtag #StarsStripes&FridayNightLights

item.title: How the Ball Bounces with Bekka: Nobody Wins the First Practice
item.dc:creator: Bekka Wilkerson
item.category: How the Ball Bounces with Bekka
item.description: Back to school has always been one of my favorite times of the year. While it marks the first official end of summer – something I don’t necessarily relish – it also brings around a whole world of new beginnings. New shoes. New Outfits. New Backpacks. item.content:encoded:
Back to school has always been one of my favorite times of the year. While it marks the first official end of summer – something I don’t necessarily relish – it also brings around a whole world of new beginnings.  

New shoes. New Outfits.  New Backpacks.  The anticipation of a new school year.

But also…a fresh uniform…striped fields…the sound of a basketball bouncing and the smell of the freshly refinished hardwood floor.

Whistles that have been hanging silent all summer finally finding their way back around a coach’s neck. Parents unfolding lawn chairs they swear they put away just a few weeks ago.

And kids…kids who somehow grew three inches since school let out.

Across Arkansas this week, athletes are walking into their first practices of a brand-new season.

Some are excited.

Some are nervous.

Some are wondering if they still remember how to play.

Some are wondering if they belong at all.

And every single one of them is starting in exactly the same place.

Practice.

Not a championship. Not a playoff game. Not Senior Night.

Practice.

The funny thing is…nobody wins the first practice.

There isn’t a trophy waiting at the end. Nobody hangs a banner because everybody survived day one of conditioning, or what feels like day 5000 of conditioning.

Nobody earns a state championship because they had a great August.

The first practice isn’t about proving anything. It’s about preparing for everything.

I remember that feeling.  Even though it was our “job” to stay in the groove all summer with conditioning and shooting, walking into the gym after a summer away always brought a mix of coming home and apprehension.  

Wondering if my shot would still be there…if I had done enough during the offseason…would Coach think I had done enough in the off season…

Because here’s the truth every athlete eventually learns: The season doesn’t begin on opening night. It begins long before anyone is keeping score. It begins in ordinary practices.

In line drills.

In stretching.

In learning names.

In figuring out who encourages teammates…and who hangs their head when things get hard.

READ MORE BELOW




The first practice tells you almost nothing about how the season will end but everything about who you are and who you will become as a team as the season progresses.

I’ve seen kids struggle through the first week of practice and become incredible players by the end of the year. I’ve seen the most naturally talented athletes lose their spot because they lost their fire and stopped putting in the work. And I’ve seen teammates who barely played become the heart of a team simply because everyone knew they could be counted on.

The first practice doesn’t reveal talent nearly as much as it reveals attitude.

The older I’ve gotten, the more I’ve realized life gives us first practices all the time.

The first day at a new job.

The first board meeting.

The first day of school.

The first time you volunteer.

The first time you decide to get healthy.

The first conversation after deciding to repair a relationship.

None of those moments determine the outcome, they simply mark the beginning. What really matters is what happens after everyone else goes home.

The showing up.

The consistency.

The willingness to keep coming back when the excitement wears off and the work begins. Because that’s when seasons are really built.

Not under Friday night lights. Not in championship games. Not when everybody is watching. But on ordinary afternoons…when nobody is keeping score.

Maybe that’s why nobody wins the first practice.

The victory isn’t in what happens that day.

The victory is deciding you’ll come back tomorrow.

And the next day.

And the day after that.

Because championships are never won in the first practice. But they can absolutely be lost by deciding it wasn’t important.

And that’s how the ball really bounces.

Read more from How the Ball Bounces with Bekka in the archives at www.mysaline.com/bounces.

About the author: Bekka Wilkerson is a lifelong lover of all things sports. Raised in a super athletic household it was no surprise when she too began to love sports at a young age. It seems like from the time she could walk she had a softball bat in her hands, but her true athletic passion came from all things Basketball. That love served her well as a Bryant High School Lady Hornet and ultimately earned her a full scholarship to play at the University of Central Arkansas – among many other adventures.
These days Bekka can be found running around Saline County with her husband, Speedy, or chasing one of her grandsons. She is also the Executive Director of The EMpact One Foundation, a Saline County Nonprofit Organization that helps young people stay connected to extracurricular activities through tuition assistance and equipment provisions.
Reach out to Bekka with questions and/or ideas about things you want to see in this column at bekka00@hotmail.com and learn more about The EMpact One Foundation at www.empactone.org.
